{# Social and search metadata. LinkedIn's post inspector, Slack, X and Google all want the same things: an absolute og:image at least 1200x627, an absolute og:url, and a title and description that say what the page is. Everything below is derived from the page and mkdocs.yml, so a page only needs to override `description` (and, rarely, `og_image`) in its front matter. The card is 2400x1260 - twice the 1200x630 that LinkedIn, Slack and X crop to - and is rendered from docs/img/og-card.svg. The file name carries the size so that a change to the artwork is a new URL, which is what makes the crawlers refetch instead of serving their cached copy. #} {% extends "base.html" %} {% block extrahead %} {# Inside the app, the app's own bar already carries the logo, the search box and the repository link, so this page's copy of them is a second row saying the same thing - and one of the two search boxes searches only half of what the reader wants. The bar is hidden when framed; the section tabs below it stay, because they are this site's own navigation and nothing in the app replaces them. Framed-ness is `window.self !== window.top`, which is true only when a page is actually inside a frame - the published site is not, and keeps its bar. The app sets the same class itself when it frames a page: a deployment's Content-Security-Policy refuses inline scripts, and the class has to be set either way. #} {# The docs are read in two places: published on their own, and framed by the app that serves them. The app has a colour-scheme setting of its own, and the Material palette below follows the OPERATING SYSTEM's preference - so a reader in dark mode got a dark app around a light page. The frame is same-origin, so the app's choice is in localStorage and can be read here. It is written in Material's own form - `__palette` names an entry in this file's palette list - because Material resolves its palette in its own script, after this one: setting the attribute here would be overwritten by the very script that decides the scheme. Standalone, the reader's own choice wins: Material persists it in `__palette` and applies it itself, so this script must not overwrite that - the toggle would appear to do nothing after a reload. Only when there is no stored choice does the operating system answer, which is what a first visit should do. The app also posts its mode on load and on every change, for the case where the reader switches while the page is open. #} {% set meta = page.meta if page and page.meta else {} %} {% set site = config.site_name %} {% set page_title = page.title if page and page.title else site %} {% set og_title = meta.og_title if meta.og_title else (site if page_title == site else page_title ~ " - " ~ site) %} {% set og_desc = meta.description if meta.description else config.site_description %} {% set og_image = meta.og_image if meta.og_image else 'img/og-card-2400.png' %} {% if not og_image.startswith('http') %} {% set og_image = config.site_url ~ og_image.lstrip('/') %} {% endif %} {% set canonical = page.canonical_url if page and page.canonical_url else config.site_url %} {% if not meta.og_image %} {% endif %} {% endblock %}
